# PinnacleAI® guided explanation
An illustrative guide to the documented workflow; no child data, assessment or product recording.
Start with everyday life.
A family wants to help their child express a choice during a familiar routine. They describe what the child already does, what interests them and where support helps.
Everyday observations give the care team context.
Source: https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/md5.html

Bring the observations together.
The family and professionals review the starting point and agree a useful goal. Pinnacle describes the Personal Development Kernel as the child-specific record connecting measurements, context and responses.
The care team checks the goal and the support appropriate to this child.
Source: https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/dossier.html

Make the starting point understandable.
The overall AbilityScore® report and seven readiness views help organise the discussion. The important connection is from the report to an agreed everyday goal.
Explore what each report is for below. No individual child’s results are displayed here.
Source: https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/methodology.html

Turn the goal into guided practice.
The documented Everyday Therapy™ programme links selected techniques with goals. In this illustration, the care team explains a communication activity within a familiar routine and agrees how the family can take part.
The activity, support and practice schedule are agreed with the care team.
Source: https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/september-handout.html

What happened during practice?
Feedback connects the experience at home with the next review. Try either response to see how the discussion can change.
This demonstration does not assess a child, prescribe an activity or generate a treatment plan.
Source: https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/dossier.html

Use the experience to shape the next plan.
The care team reviews feedback, adjusts goals or support, and discusses the next assessment. Monthly reassessment is described in the reviewed methodology and walkthrough.
Look for meaningful changes in communication, routines, learning and participation, alongside the scores.
Source: https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/methodology.html

Report explorer
AbilityScore® / TherapeuticAI® report: The overall developmental profile.
Question for the care team: Which abilities should we prioritise, and why?

Speech Readiness Index: A focused view to discuss communication priorities.
Question for the care team: How can we support communication in everyday routines?

Behavior Readiness Index: A focused view to discuss behaviour and participation.
Question for the care team: What helps my child feel comfortable and take part?

Motor Readiness Index: A focused view to discuss movement-related abilities.
Question for the care team: Which movement skills matter for my child’s routines?

Study/IQ Readiness Index: The report’s named view of readiness for learning.
Question for the care team: What support could make learning more accessible?

School Readiness Index: A focused view to discuss preparation and support for school.
Question for the care team: What would help my child participate at school?

Self-Sufficiency Index: A focused view to discuss growing everyday independence.
Question for the care team: Which everyday task could my child do with less help?

Mainstream Readiness Index: A focused view to discuss participation with other people.
Question for the care team: What support would help my child join in with others?
